## Derivation

**Reformulation.** $S\cap(S+k)\neq\emptyset$ holds iff there exist $s,t\in S$ with $s=t+k$, i.e. $k\in S-S$. So the condition is exactly $S-S=\mathbf{Z}_n$, and $f(n)$ is the minimum size of such an $S$.

**Lower bound.** The difference set $S-S$ is the image of the $|S|(|S|-1)$ ordered pairs of distinct elements, together with $0$. Hence
$$n=|S-S|\le |S|(|S|-1)+1,$$
so $|S|\ge \sqrt{n}-\tfrac12$ roughly, giving $f(n)\ge \sqrt{n}-1$ for all $n\ge 2$.

**Upper bound.** Let $m=\lceil\sqrt n\,\rceil$, so $m^2\ge n$. Take
$$S=\{0,1,\dots,m-1\}\cup\{0,m,2m,\dots,(m-1)m\}\subset\mathbf{Z}_n,$$
with $|S|\le 2m$. For $b,a\in\{0,\dots,m-1\}$, the differences $bm-a$ are integers. As $b$ runs over $0,\dots,m-1$, the intervals $[bm-(m-1),\,bm]$ join into the contiguous integer range $[-(m-1),\,m^2-m]$, which has length at least $m^2\ge n$. Reducing mod $n$ therefore covers all of $\mathbf{Z}_n$, so $S-S=\mathbf{Z}_n$. Hence $f(n)\le 2\lceil\sqrt n\rceil$.

**Conclusion.** For all $n\ge 2$,
$$\sqrt{n}-1\le f(n)\le 2\sqrt{n}+2.$$
Taking logarithms and dividing by $\ln n$:
$$\frac{\ln f(n)}{\ln n}\to\frac12,$$
since $\ln(c\sqrt n)/\ln n = \tfrac12 + \ln c/\ln n\to\tfrac12$ for any fixed constant $c>0$.

No domain restrictions beyond $n\ge 2$ were needed, and the quantifiers are satisfied: the construction gives $S-S=\mathbf{Z}_n$ for every $n$, and the counting bound applies to every such $S$.

Final answer: 1/2
